Trauma, Stress and Dissociative Disorders

acute stress disorder · posttraumatic stress disorder · adjustment disorder · dissociative disordersTrauma or stressor, and how long since?

Practice
  1. 35-year-old man seen 2 weeks after a highway crash that killed the other driver wakes from dreams of the crash; jumps at car horns feels unreal, as if watching himself; will not drive no drug use; examination normal → Acute stress disorder → a trauma, then intrusion, arousal, avoidance and dissociation 2 weeks later: acute stress disorder, 3 days to 1 month after the trauma; PTSD needs symptoms over 1 month, and dissociation inside an acute stress picture is not a separate disorder
  2. 9-year-old girl brought by her grandmother, who gained custody 2 years ago as a toddler she was left alone for days without food or heat nightmares, startles easily, hits classmates, will not sleep alone growth and examination normal → Posttraumatic stress disorder → severe neglect, then nightmares, startle, aggression and avoidance far longer than 1 month: PTSD; with trauma and intrusion, aggression is more likely PTSD arousal than oppositional defiant disorder
  3. 41-year-old man laid off from his job 5 weeks ago tearful, sleeping poorly, cannot focus on job applications still enjoys time with his children; no guilt or thoughts of death energy and appetite normal; no past mood episodes → Adjustment disorder with depressed mood → a non-traumatic stressor 5 weeks ago and fewer than 5 depressive symptoms: adjustment disorder with depressed mood; major depressive disorder needs 5 or more, and persistent depressive disorder needs 2 years
  4. 20-year-old college student whose parents announced their divorce 1 month ago worried and restless; cannot sit through lectures grades slipping; sleeps adequately; eats normally no past anxiety; no substance use; vital signs and examination normal → Adjustment disorder with anxiety → anxiety and impaired function within 3 months of a non-traumatic stressor, short of another disorder: adjustment disorder with anxiety; generalized anxiety needs 6 months or more, and acute stress disorder needs a life-threatening trauma
  5. 33-year-old firefighter treated for PTSD after a fatal building collapse flashbacks and avoidance much improved after CBT and 5 months of sertraline still wakes most nights from vivid dreams of the collapse blood pressure 124/78 mm Hg; drinks rarely → Add prazosin at bedtime → PTSD better on CBT and an SSRI but nightmares persist: add prazosin, an alpha-1 blocker, titrated for blood pressure; a benzodiazepine does not help the nightmares, and switching a working SSRI risks relapse
  6. 50-year-old woman found by police at a bus station 300 miles from home cannot give her name, address or job; attention and reasoning intact her son died suddenly 2 days earlier urine toxicology negative; neurologic examination normal → Dissociative amnesia with fugue → lost identity and personal history after a stressor, with travel, intact cognition and no substance or neurologic cause: dissociative amnesia with fugue; transient global amnesia keeps identity, and dissociative identity disorder needs 2 or more identities
  7. 24-year-old graduate student with months of recurrent episodes of feeling detached says she watches herself from outside, as if in a film knows the feeling is not real; memory for events intact no drug use; neurologic examination normal → Depersonalization/derealization disorder → recurrent detachment from herself with reality testing and memory intact, and no substance or neurologic cause: depersonalization/derealization disorder; intact reality testing rules out psychosis, and intact memory rules out dissociative amnesia
  8. 28-year-old woman seen 10 days after being sexually assaulted nightmares, startles easily, avoids the street where it happened feels numb and in a fog much of the day no suicidal thoughts; no substance use; examination normal → Trauma-focused CBT → acute stress disorder 10 days after a sexual assault: trauma-focused CBT first, started early to lower the risk of PTSD; drugs are typically not needed, and prazosin is an adjunct for PTSD nightmares that persist on an SSRI
Pairs with Major Depressive Disorder covers a full depressive episode after a loss. Psychosis covers brief psychotic disorder, often after a stressor. Cluster B Personality Disorders covers borderline personality and childhood trauma. Cluster C Personality Disorders covers dependent personality.
Transferable rule

After a trauma or stressor, ask what it was and how long since: a life-threatening trauma 3 days to 1 month after the trauma is acute stress disorder and over 1 month is PTSD; any other stressor, with symptoms short of another disorder, is adjustment disorder.
